briefing.title: Briefing after cycle 012 — what the world is pressing on

lines.text: UCDP counted about 244,600 people killed in organised violence in 2025, up from about 187,000 in 2024, and a record 65 state-based conflicts.
lines.say: The Uppsala Conflict Data Program counted about two hundred and forty-four thousand six hundred people killed in organised violence in twenty twenty-five, up from about one hundred and eighty-seven thousand in twenty twenty-four, and a record sixty-five state-based conflicts.

lines.text: SIPRI put world military spending at $2,887 billion in 2025, up 2.9% in real terms.
lines.say: SIPRI put world military spending at two thousand eight hundred and eighty-seven billion dollars in twenty twenty-five, up two point nine percent in real terms.

sources.label: Uppsala University, UCDP press release on the 2025 data, 9 June 2026
Davies, Pettersson and Öberg, Organized violence 1989–2025, Journal of Peace Research 63(4), 2026
SIPRI, Trends in World Military Expenditure, 2025, fact sheet, April 2026

lines.text: SOFI 2026 nowcasts 645 million people undernourished in 2025 (7.8%, range 608–696 million), about 14 million fewer than in 2024.
lines.say: The State of Food Security report nowcasts six hundred and forty-five million people undernourished in twenty twenty-five, seven point eight percent, in a range of six hundred and eight to six hundred and ninety-six million, about fourteen million fewer than in twenty twenty-four.

lines.text: Separately, 266 million people in 47 food-crisis countries and territories faced high acute food insecurity in 2025, 22.9% of those analysed.
lines.say: Separately, two hundred and sixty-six million people in forty-seven food-crisis countries and territories faced high acute food insecurity in twenty twenty-five, twenty-two point nine percent of those analysed.

sources.label: FAO, IFAD, UNICEF, WFP and WHO, The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World 2026, 21 July 2026

lines.text: The World Bank nowcasts about 811 million people, 1 in 10, below $3.00 a day (2021 PPP) in 2026; 2024, the latest year with sufficient data, stands at 824 million.
lines.say: The World Bank's now cast is about eight hundred and eleven million people, one in ten, below three dollars a day in twenty twenty-six; twenty twenty-four, the latest year with sufficient data, stands at eight hundred and twenty-four million.

lines.text: UNDP and OPHI count 1.2 billion (18.9%) in acute multidimensional poverty in 108 countries, surveys of 2014–2025.
lines.say: The United Nations Development Programme and Oxford's poverty initiative count one point two billion people, eighteen point nine percent, in acute multidimensional poverty in one hundred and eight countries, in surveys from twenty fourteen to twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: The World Bank counts 824 million people in extreme poverty in 2024, below three dollars a day.
lines.say: The World Bank counts eight hundred and twenty-four million people in extreme poverty in twenty twenty-four, below three dollars a day.

lines.text: Its nowcast falls only from 10.1 to 9.8 percent by 2026.
lines.say: Its now cast falls only from ten point one to nine point eight percent by twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: Extreme poverty is rising in the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan, and remains high in Sub-Saharan Africa.

channels.title: Debt, work and cost of living

lines.text: UNCTAD counts 3.7 billion people in 51 developing countries that spend more on interest than on health or on education, 1.2 billion more than in 2010.
lines.say: UN Trade and Development counts three point seven billion people in fifty-one developing countries that spend more on interest than on health or on education, one point two billion more than in twenty ten.

lines.text: Developing countries' net interest bill on public debt reached $995 billion in 2025.
lines.say: Developing countries' net interest bill on public debt reached nine hundred and ninety-five billion dollars in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: The IMF projects world inflation of 4.7% in 2026, up from 4.1% in 2025, driven by energy and food prices.
lines.say: The International Monetary Fund projects world inflation of four point seven percent in twenty twenty-six, up from four point one percent in twenty twenty-five, driven by energy and food prices.

lines.text: UNCTAD counts 3.7 billion people living in countries that spend more on interest than on health or on education.
lines.say: UN Trade and Development counts three point seven billion people living in countries that spend more on interest than on health or on education.

lines.text: That is 1.2 billion more people than in 2010.
lines.say: That is one point two billion more people than in twenty ten.

lines.text: Developing countries paid $995 billion in net interest on public debt in 2025.
lines.say: Developing countries paid nine hundred and ninety-five billion dollars in net interest on public debt in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: In Africa, the share of people in such countries rose from 24 to 65 percent between 2010 and 2023.
lines.say: In Africa, the share of people in such countries rose from twenty-four to sixty-five percent between twenty ten and twenty twenty-three.

sources.label: UNCTAD, A World of Debt 2026
IMF, World Economic Outlook, October 2026: Resilience Under Strain, Urgent Choices, 13 October 2026
IMF, World Economic Outlook Update, July 2026

lines.text: World Inequality Lab estimates, 2025: the global top 10% took 53% of income and held 75% of wealth, the bottom half 8% and 2%.
lines.say: World Inequality Lab estimates for twenty twenty-five: the global top ten percent took fifty-three percent of income and held seventy-five percent of wealth, the bottom half eight percent and two percent.

lines.text: The top 0.001% held nearly 6.1% of wealth, up from around 3.8% in 1995.
lines.say: The top zero point zero zero one percent held nearly six point one percent of wealth, up from around three point eight percent in nineteen ninety-five.

lines.text: Average income in North America & Oceania is about 13 times Sub-Saharan Africa's.
lines.say: Average income in North America and Oceania is about thirteen times Sub-Saharan Africa's.

lines.text: By the World Inequality Lab's estimates for 2025, the richest tenth held 75 percent of the world's wealth.
lines.say: By the World Inequality Lab's estimates for twenty twenty-five, the richest tenth held seventy-five percent of the world's wealth.

lines.text: The poorer half held 2 percent.
lines.say: The poorer half held two percent.

lines.text: The top 0.001 percent held nearly 6.1 percent, up from around 3.8 percent in 1995.
lines.say: The top zero point zero zero one percent held nearly six point one percent, up from around three point eight percent in nineteen ninety-five.

lines.text: Epoch AI estimates that five hyperscalers held 71% of the world's cumulative AI compute at the end of 2025, up from 63% early in 2024.
lines.say: Epoch AI estimates that five hyperscalers held seventy-one percent of the world's cumulative AI compute at the end of twenty twenty-five, up from sixty-three percent early in twenty twenty-four.

lines.text: Google took 89.94% of worldwide search referrals in September 2026, by StatCounter's count of page views.
lines.say: Google took eighty-nine point nine four percent of worldwide search referrals in September twenty twenty-six, by StatCounter's count of page views.

lines.text: Epoch AI estimates Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle held 71 percent of the world's AI compute at the end of 2025.
lines.say: Epoch AI estimates Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle held seventy-one percent of the world's AI compute at the end of twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: Early in 2024 the five held 63 percent.
lines.say: Early in twenty twenty-four the five held sixty-three percent.

lines.text: It is an estimate, measured in a common unit of chips, on incomplete records of who owns them.

lines.text: October 2026 was the warmest October on record, 1.75°C above the pre-industrial level, the third month in a row above 1.5°C.
lines.say: October twenty twenty-six was the warmest October on record, one point seven five degrees above the pre-industrial level, the third month in a row above one and a half degrees.

lines.text: The twelve months to October averaged 1.51°C, and an exceptionally strong El Niño was still strengthening.
lines.say: The twelve months to October averaged one point five one degrees, and an exceptionally strong El Niño was still strengthening.

lines.text: October 2026 was the warmest October on record, 1.75°C above the pre-industrial level.
lines.say: October twenty twenty-six was the warmest October on record, one point seven five degrees above the pre-industrial level.

lines.text: It was the third month in a row above one and a half degrees.
Sea surface temperatures outside the poles set an October record, as an exceptionally strong El Niño kept strengthening.
Copernicus expects 2026 as a whole to exceed 1.5°C.
lines.say: Copernicus expects twenty twenty-six as a whole to exceed one and a half degrees.

lines.text: COP31 runs in Antalya, Türkiye, from 9 to 20 November 2026.
lines.say: COP thirty-one runs in Antalya, Türkiye, from the ninth to the twentieth of November twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: UNEP finds that current policies could take warming to 2.8°C this century.
lines.say: The UN Environment Programme finds that current policies could take warming to two point eight degrees this century.

lines.text: If every national pledge is met, warming is limited to 2.6°C.
lines.say: If every national pledge is met, warming is limited to two point six degrees.

lines.text: The outlook is worse than last year's, after the United States left the Paris Agreement.

lines.text: The Planetary Health Check finds seven of nine planetary boundaries transgressed, all at their highest recorded level.
lines.say: The Planetary Health Check finds seven of nine planetary boundaries transgressed, all at their highest recorded level.

lines.text: Air pollution contributed to 7.9 million deaths in 2023, by the State of Global Air's estimate.

lines.text: Air pollution contributed to 7.9 million deaths in 2023, by the State of Global Air's estimate.
lines.say: Air pollution contributed to seven point nine million deaths in twenty twenty-three, by the State of Global Air's estimate.

lines.text: 4.9 million were attributed to fine particles outdoors, 2.8 million to household air pollution.

lines.text: UN estimates say 4.9 million children died before age five in 2024, and the pace of decline has slowed by 61%.
lines.say: United Nations estimates say four point nine million children died before age five in twenty twenty-four, and the pace of decline has slowed by sixty-one percent.

lines.say: Congo's Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak had ten thousand, six hundred and sixty-eight confirmed cases, including five thousand, one hundred and ninety-eight deaths, by the third of November twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: UNHCR estimates 117.8 million people were forcibly displaced at the end of 2025, 5.4 million fewer than a year earlier.
lines.say: The UN refugee agency estimates one hundred and seventeen point eight million people were forcibly displaced at the end of twenty twenty-five, five point four million fewer than a year earlier.

lines.text: RSF's 2026 index (covering 2025) rates press freedom "difficult" or "very serious" in 52.2% of 180 countries and territories, against 13.7% in 2002.
lines.say: The twenty twenty-six index of Reporters Without Borders, covering twenty twenty-five, rates press freedom difficult or very serious in fifty-two point two percent of one hundred and eighty countries and territories, against thirteen point seven percent in two thousand and two.

lines.text: In the 2026 Digital News Report survey, trust in news averaged 37% across 48 markets, the lowest since measuring began in 2015.
